headline: Anthropic wants Claude to analyze your bank account and financial data
notes: Vendor product test ("Claude Money"). The actor is the model provider, not a bank, and no institution is named as running it.

headline: SA banks put AI value under the microscope
notes: Sector survey of South African banks. Real adoption is described in aggregate; no single institution, process or outcome is named, so there is no use case to fold.

headline: UOB commits S$500,000 to equip 1,000 children with AI skills
notes: Corporate philanthropy. A bank is the actor and AI is the subject, and it is still not a bank applying AI to a bank process. The gate cannot see this distinction; a reader can.

headline: Banks Use AI Agents to Catch Compliance Drift Earlier
task: monitoring compliance drift in transaction monitoring rules
notes: Named vendor with named bank deployments and a stated process. Graded A on the process, not the vendor; the actor is Flagright because the piece names no single bank.

headline: State bank examiners get a playbook for inspecting AI
notes: Supervisory guidance. Regulator-side, and about how to inspect AI rather than an institution running it. Consistent with pass 14: a supervisor is graded A only when the supervisor itself runs the process.

headline: Mastercard and Trip.com target travel sector agentic commerce
task: agentic booking and payment in travel
notes: Named first party, named product, named process. A showcase rather than a rollout, so pilot rather than in_production.

headline: With Claude for Financial Advisors, Anthropic Reflects AI's Potential in Wealth
notes: Commentary on a vendor launch. Same story and same grade as the two already recorded in pass 17.

headline: Can 'Role-Playing' AI Agents Change The Game for Advisor Education?
notes: Training simulators for advisers. Trade-press exploration of a category, no institution named as running it.

headline: Anthropic Just Broke Down the Cost Barrier to Agentic Commerce
notes: Vendor capability commentary. Community post on a vendor release.

headline: A.I. Meets Wealth Management via SS&C, Anthropic & OpenAI
notes: Vendor partnership announcement. SS&C is the supplier; no wealth manager is named as running it.

headline: Would you let AI spend your money? The trust issue facing agentic payments
notes: Opinion piece by a community member. Commentary on a category.

headline: Bank of Georgia: AI-Native Infrastructure and the Future of Digital Banking
notes: Interview with the bank's own chief digital officer describing what the bank runs. Process corrected from P35 to P5: super-apps and customer-facing financial agents are servicing, not platform engineering.

headline: Everything we know so far about Anthropic's 'Claude for financial advisers'
notes: Fourth report of the vendor launch. Same grade as the three before it.

headline: OpenAI Expands Board With Fintech, Banking Leaders Ahead Of Potential IPO

headline: Portfolio reviews, client meeting prep: Anthropic launches Claude tool for financial advisers
notes: Fifth report of the vendor launch.

headline: PicPay Launches Anthropic Claude Integration for Banking Inquiries
notes: Named institution, named model, named process, launched. The bank is the actor and the model is the tool, which is the distinction that separates this from the five B-graded Anthropic launches above.

headline: FI Works launches AI-driven analytics
notes: Vendor launch for community banks. No named institution running it.

headline: Standard Bank Group Technology Hackathon 2026 gets underway
notes: A hackathon is an event, not a process. Same reasoning as the UOB philanthropy piece above.

task: search, account inquiries and transfers in the banking app
notes: Second report of KB AI. Folds with 아시아경제 and 헤럴드경제.

headline: AXA Hong Kong brings artificial intelligence into underwriting
notes: Insurer applying AI to insurance underwriting. Regraded from A: this is a bank process landscape, and insurance underwriting is not one of its processes. Forcing it into P26 credit and counterparty risk made the taxonomy claim something it does not mean.

headline: 7 Best Practices for Delivering Superior Customer Experience in AI-Driven AML and Fraud Prevention
notes: Best-practice listicle. Advice, not a deployment.

headline: AI in Asset Management Has Made It More Homogeneous
notes: Analysis of an effect across the industry. Genuinely about AI in asset management, and no institution or process to attribute.

headline: Palantir upgraded to Buy by UBS on strong AI and data demand
notes: Equity research. UBS is the analyst, not the operator — exactly the false positive the commentary gate exists for, and it slipped through because both `palantir` and `ubs` now match. Worth watching: this is the first cost of adding `palantir`.

headline: Shinhan Bank joins Kakao consortium in AI for All project
notes: Consortium membership to develop future services. No process is running yet; announced-stage collaboration without a named use case.

headline: Zopa launches AI-powered 'Ask Zopa' for conversational banking
task: conversational banking assistant answering customer questions
notes: Named bank, named product, launched. This is the story the rejection report flagged as a miss under a different headline — it arrived twice through other feeds, so nothing was lost.

headline: The National Bank to implement AI and big data technologies for banking supervision
actor: National Bank of the Kyrgyz Republic
notes: A supervisor running a process on itself, which pass 14 established is graded A. Announced rather than live.

headline: KB Kookmin Bank launches 'KB AI' service for financial searches and transfers
task: search, account inquiries and transfers in the banking app
notes: Third report of KB AI. All three fold to one use case.

notes: Cost commentary by a community member.

notes: Second report of Ask Zopa. Folds with the IBS Intelligence report.

notes: Vendor partnership announcement with no institution named as running it. Regraded from A for consistency: four identical vendor launches in this same batch are B, and I had no reason to treat this one differently.

notes: Vendor launch aimed at banks. No named bank running it.

headline: Revolut and N26 Alumni Launch Quartz: The AI Personal Banker Secures £2.75M Pre-Seed
notes: Startup funding. Revolut and N26 appear only as the founders' former employers — a named-institution false positive worth noting.

headline: Personetics Launches Banking Console, Bringing AI-Powered Customer Intelligence to the Relationship Manager's Desktop
notes: Vendor launch. Named product and named process, but no institution running it.

headline: The Central Bank will continue to implement AI in financial services
notes: Statement of intent from a central bank with no named process. Distinguished from the Kyrgyz supervisor above, which names banking supervision as the process.

headline: JPMorgan's Private Bank Reset Targets the Next Wave of AI Wealth
notes: About serving clients who made their money in AI, not about the bank using AI. A headline that reads as adoption and is not — the reverse of the Zopa case, and a reminder that the gate cannot substitute for reading.

headline: ByteDance arrangiert einen Kredit in Höhe von 29,6 Milliarden US-Dollar für KI-Ausbaupläne
notes: Corporate borrowing to fund AI infrastructure. Admitted by the new `kredit` term. This is the thin call the term list flagged in advance; one instance is not yet grounds to drop it, but it is the first.

headline: US Defense Department weighs $5b loan for AI startup Fluidstack
notes: Government lending to an AI company. Admitted by `loan`. Same shape as the ByteDance piece: AI capital news, not AI in banking.

headline: FCA boss warns laws can never keep up with AI
notes: Regulator commentary. Admitted by the new `fca` term, and correctly — it is AI-in-banking news, and it is not a use case.

headline: US Treasury Releases Report On The Uses, Opportunities, And Risks Of Artificial Intelligence In Financial Services
notes: Policy report. Two years old, arriving through GDELT; graded on content rather than age.
